newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil May Fipe inflation at 0.55 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil May Fipe inflation at 0.55 pct.

text.p: Brazil's inflation as measured by the Economic Research Institute (Fipe) was 0.55 percent in May versus 0.64 percent in April, a Fipe official said.
Fipe chief Juarez Rizzieri said a fall in food prices caused the slowing in the price index, which measures inflation in the Sao Paulo area.
He expected inflation to pick up again in June due to a rise in bus and telephone prices.
Rizzieri released the following breakdown of Fipe's weighted inflation index for May.
- Food -1.37 pct drop in the month
- Housing 1.96 pct rise in the month
- Transportation 0.02 pct rise in the month
- Personal expenses -0.41 pct drop in the month
- Clothing 5.30 pct rise in the month
- Health care 1.22 pct rise in the month
- Education 0.12 pct rise in the mont
The Fipe index is calculated by the University of Sao Paulo, which releases inflation figures weekly.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
